stem: Look at the labeled microscope. Which number points to the part you look through?
explanation: Number 1 is the ocular lens (eyepiece). You look through it, and it usually magnifies 10×.

stem: Look at the labeled microscope. Which number points to the part that holds the slide?
explanation: Number 3 is the stage, the flat platform that holds the slide under the objective lens.

stem: Look at the labeled microscope. Which number points to the objective lenses, the lenses closest to the slide?
explanation: Number 2 points to the objective lenses on the nosepiece, just above the slide.

stem: Look at the labeled microscope. A student is on low power and can't see the specimen yet. Which numbered knob should the student turn first to bring it into focus?
explanation: Number 4 is the coarse adjustment knob. It moves the stage a lot, so use it first on low power.

stem: Look at the labeled microscope. After switching to high power, which numbered knob is the only one you should use to sharpen the focus?
explanation: Number 5 is the fine adjustment knob. On high power use only the fine knob; the coarse knob can crash the lens into the slide.

stem: Look at the labeled microscope. What is the job of the part labeled 3?
option_a: It holds the slide under the lenses
option_c: It moves the stage a lot to focus on low power
option_d: It controls how much light reaches the specimen
explanation: Part 3 is the stage. It holds the slide; the lenses (1 and 2) magnify and the knobs (4 and 5) focus.

stem: Look at the labeled microscope. Part 1 magnifies 10×, and the lens at part 2 that is in place magnifies 40×. What is the total magnification?
explanation: Multiply the ocular (part 1) by the objective (part 2): 10 × 40 = 400×.

stem: Look at the labeled microscope. A student on high power turns part 4 and cracks the slide. What should the student have done instead?
option_b: Turned part 5, the fine adjustment knob
explanation: Part 4 is the coarse knob, which moves too far on high power. On high power, focus only with part 5, the fine adjustment knob.
